field.label: Buyer reference (Leitweg-ID)
field.helpText: The buyer's own reference — for a German public-sector buyer this is usually a Leitweg-ID. Used as BT-10 ("Buyer reference") on an EN 16931 export; XRechnung's own BR-DE-15 refuses the document when this is missing (`formats/xrechnung-provider.ts`).

field.label: Supply type
field.helpText: Whether this line is a delivery of goods or a supply of services — it decides how a cross-border sale is taxed. Goods sold to a consumer in another EU member state are an intra-Community distance sale, taxed where they arrive once your EU-wide distance sales pass EUR 10 000 in a calendar year (Directive 2006/112/EC art. 33(a) and art. 59c); the same sale as a service stays taxable here (art. 45). Optional: a line that declares nothing is treated as a supply of services.

notes: Germany's FIRST field-overlay file — same mechanism and shape as France's own `fr.json` (`lines[].supplyType`), applied here at the DOCUMENT level instead of a line: BT-10 ("Buyer reference") is a document-wide fact, not a per-line one. Added as an OPTIONAL top-level field (`path: ''` — schema.ts's own top-level convention) rather than a change to the trunk `invoice.descriptor.ts`: BT-10 only becomes MANDATORY under the XRechnung/Peppol deltas (`formats/xrechnung-provider.ts`'s BR-DE-15, `formats/peppol-bis-provider.ts`'s PEPPOL-EN16931-R003), never at the base EN 16931 layer every OTHER seller builds against — the same 'a country's own difference from the trunk is data, never a change forced on everyone' discipline `country-fields/schema.ts`'s own header documents. `formats/shared-build.ts#extractBuyerReference` reads `data.buyerReference` generically, off ANY document regardless of which overlay (if any) put an input for it on screen — see that function's own header: a seller in a country with no overlay for this field (e.g. a French seller invoicing a German public body, the exact case XRechnung exists for) has no SCREEN control for it today, a known, documented UX gap, not a format that refuses to serve them — the underlying JSON value, however it got there, is read the same way for every seller. Labeled directly (no i18n key), matching every other field label already shipped on `fr.json`'s own `supplyType` overlay and `invoice.descriptor.ts` itself — see that file's own comment on `DocumentFieldDescriptor.label` for why the frontend renders it verbatim, never through `t()`. SECOND OPERATION, added later: the SAME `supplyType` line subfield France's own `fr.json` already adds, byte-identical in key, kind, label, options and optionality — a LINE subfield, unlike `buyerReference` above. WHY THE FIELD IS IDENTICAL IN ALL FIVE COUNTRIES RATHER THAN A PER-COUNTRY VARIANT: what reads it — `tax/resolve-invoice-tax.ts`, feeding `tax/tax-engine.ts#determineLineTax` — branches on the goods/services distinction of Directive 2006/112/EC (arts. 32, 33(a) and 59c for an intra-Community distance sale of goods, art. 45 for a service), which binds every member state identically; the same reasoning `tax/types.ts`'s own `DistanceSalesRegime` states for art. 59c ('art. 59c applies identically in all of them'). Germany's transposition defines the two in the directive's own terms — « Lieferungen eines Unternehmers sind Leistungen, durch die er oder in seinem Auftrag ein Dritter den Abnehmer oder in dessen Auftrag einen Dritten befähigt, im eigenen Namen über einen Gegenstand zu verfügen (Verschaffung der Verfügungsmacht) » (UStG § 3 Abs. 1) against « Sonstige Leistungen sind Leistungen, die keine Lieferungen sind. Sie können auch in einem Unterlassen oder im Dulden einer Handlung oder eines Zustands bestehen » (UStG § 3 Abs. 9), the residual definition the directive itself uses. Read in raw text on 2026-09-21 at gesetze-im-internet.de (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustg_1980/__3.html). WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED FROM FRANCE: the French overlay's own `helpText` names BT-23 (« cadre de facturation »), which is a FRENCH obligation — `formats/semantic/business-process.ts#resolveFrenchBusinessProcessCode` derives that code only for a seller whose country has an active BT-23 rule in `content-requirements/`, and France is the only country with one — so a German seller declaring a supply type changes the exported document not at all; it changes the TAX determination, which is what this operation's own help text names instead. NO RETROACTIVE EFFECT ON STORED DOCUMENTS: the field is OPTIONAL and nothing back-fills it. `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a line's raw `supplyType` to GOODS/SERVICES and treats anything else — including absent — as SERVICES, emitting a named warning; that fallback is untouched here, so every invoice stored before this operation existed resolves exactly as it did before, and only a line a user explicitly marks as goods reaches the distance-sales branch. DIGITAL IS NOT OFFERED, on purpose: `tax/types.ts`'s own `SupplyType` has a third value, but `resolve-invoice-tax.ts` narrows a stored value to GOODS/SERVICES only, so a 'DIGITAL' option would be silently discarded on the way in — offering it would need that narrowing widened first, for all five countries including France.
